newsitem.title: NORWAY: Storebrand and Christiania to merge.
newsitem.headline: Storebrand and Christiania to merge.

text.p: Storebrand ASA, Norway's biggest insurer, and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse, the country's second biggest bank, announced on Wednesday they planned to merge.
"Storebrand and Kreditkassen (Christiania) will merge," a statement said.
It said a news conference would be held at 0800 gmt in Oslo.
Each set of shareholders will hold 50 percent of the combined group, which will be called Christiania.
The agreed exchange ratio is based on market values with two ordinary shares in Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse equivalent to one ordinary Storebrand share, a joint statement said.
The new company will be Norway's largest financial group and will be the sixth largest in the Nordic region in terms of market capitalisation.

"The merges group will be able to play a more active role in a developing Nordic market, and be better positioned for profitable growth than if each of the two groups were to remain separate, thus creating additional shareholder value," the two companies said.
The merged group will have a market capitalisation of more than 26 billion crowns, based on sharevalues at the close of trade on March 26.
Aage Korsvold, current Storebrand chief executive officer, will be CEO of the new Christiania and Harald Arnkvaern, Christiania Bank chairman will be the nominated chairman of the new board.
"I'm very confident that with this merger we will create a financial institution that is well prepared for the challenges we see ahead of us," Korsvold said in the statement.
"In a market subject to increasing competition, in particular from international players, the merged group will strengthen its position to the benefit of customers, employees and shareholders alike."

The companies said the Christiania Bank and Storebrand brands will be retained and the principal elements of the two groups' operating structures -- banking, non-life insurance, life insurance/pensions and asset management -- will be maintained.

The new group will be the leading Norwegian insurance company in both non-life and life insurance businesses and the second largest bank in Norway. The merged Christiania will have a combined market share of 32 percent in the life insurance sector, five percentage points higher than Storebrand's current position, when Christiania Bank division Norske Liv's market share is included.

In non-life insurance, the new group's share will remain at 39 percent, while it will hold a market share of about 12 percent in traditional banking products, equal to Chrisitiania Bank's current position.
